transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for making time for this calibration meeting. As you know, Taylor's annual performance review is due, and I'd like to walk through the draft together before I finalize it. The current draft flags some missed deliverables as a concern, but I also understand that several of Taylor's priorities shifted during this review cycle, so I want to make sure we account for that context. I'd like to go around and hear input from each of you — project lead, peer colleague, and HR — so we can land on a fair and accurate final rating. Let's start with the project lead's perspective.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Before I give my broader input, I need to put something on the record. My project records show that exactly six of Taylor's delayed deliverables were delayed because leadership reprioritized the work after Taylor had already started it. I haven't yet added this attribution to the calibration notes, but it's important context for assessing those missed deliverables in the draft.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I'd like to add something to the record as well. I directly observed exactly four occasions when Taylor identified a delivery risk early enough for the team to avoid an escalation. These examples haven't been collected in Taylor's review packet, but they're relevant to assessing Taylor's overall performance — particularly around risk awareness and proactive communication, which I think rounds out the picture alongside the missed deliverables and the reprioritization context Grant just shared.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share something from HR's confidential records that directly affects how we assess Taylor's deliverables. Taylor worked under an approved 80 percent schedule for two months of the review cycle. That means the performance goals for that period must be recalibrated to 80 percent of standard capacity — any deliverables assessed during those two months need to be measured against a reduced expectation, not full-time capacity. This hasn't been reflected in the draft review, and it materially affects the missed-deliverables concern that's currently flagged.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Thank you all for bringing this critical context forward. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I finalize anything. Nia, you've documented four instances of proactive risk identification that demonstrate strong risk awareness and communication — that's positive evidence that belongs in the review packet. And Owen, the approved 80 percent schedule for two months means we must recalibrate Taylor's goals for that period to 80 percent capacity — any deliverables assessed during those months need to be measured against reduced expectations. Taken together, all three of these factors materially affect the missed-deliverables concern currently flagged in the draft. I'm going to incorporate all of this into the final review: recording the six reprioritized delays as contextual attribution, including the four risk interventions as positive performance evidence, and recalibrating the goals for the 80 percent schedule period.
